(a) the HYDRA architecture provides a basis for the development of integrated, domain-oriented, collaborative design environments that can support the long-term, project-level collaboration needs of design teams, and (b) these environments can be built using the HYDRA framework.
(a) the design of a project is a distributed, asynchronous activity, and (b) the work object is a central component of this activity.

(a) the key to supporting indirect collaborative design is to provide a mechanism for the sharing of work objects; and (b) this can be accomplished by providing integrated, domain-oriented, knowledge-based design environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of design environments for supporting the work of design teams in large, complex projects.
how to support the work of design teams in a manner that is consistent with their design processes.
the following questions: What are the design issues that arise in the design of large-scale, distributed design environments?

our research has shown that a design environment can provide an effective means for the indirect coordination of the activities of project members.
the design environment approach is a promising one for supporting the long-term, collaborative design process.
our research is directed toward developing a new approach for supporting collaborative, long-term design work.

we are developing a new approach to collaborative design that is based on the integration of domain-oriented, knowledge-based design environments.
we are building a system that supports the design of computer communication networks by providing a shared design environment for the members of a distributed design team.
